title: Film the machines at Vplus Laundry, Hanoi
description:
Vplus Laundry in Hanoi runs Ecowash machines: coin-operated washers that DualMint finances and settles the cash flow from onchain. Go stand in front of them and put it on camera.

Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/Xo9APa1ZDTdsr4817

What to film
  
Record yourself at the laundromat saying, on camera: "Boring works."

Then film the place. The machines mid-cycle, the space, the signage, people coming and going, whatever detail catches your eye. The point is simple. These are real washing machines, in a real laundromat, earning real money in a real city. Boring works because the machine runs the same cycle whether crypto is up or down. Most people have never seen onchain infrastructure attached to something this ordinary. That is the whole point.

After you film

Post the video to X. Tag @DualMintRWA and @poidhxyz. Add a short caption. A thought, a reaction, something about the laundromat, the machines, or the idea of owning the cash flow without owning the machine.

To claim
  
  - Drop the link to your X post in the claim description
  - Upload a screenshot from your video as proof
  - Make sure the video clearly shows you at the laundromat
  
Bonus points for

  - Narration that tells a story
  - Capturing the atmosphere of the place
  - An interesting observation or a conversation with someone there
  - Clean editing
  - Making "machine-backed yield" feel like something you can stand next to

Housekeeping

Low-effort claims may be rejected at the reviewer's discretion. Very short clips, machines or laundromat barely visible, no commentary, or anything that doesn't actually document the location. The goal is content that genuinely shows the real-world infrastructure behind DualMint.

Respect the people there. Don't make customers or staff the focus of your video. Keep it on the machines, the space, and your own commentary. You are responsible for following local laws and the venue's rules on filming and posting.

First legit claim wins. 🏆

What is DualMint?

DualMint finances everyday machines: coin-operated laundromats, HVAC units, vending networks, arcade machines. It settles their operating revenue onchain as yield in USDC. The yield comes from quarters going into washing machines, not from token emissions or lending. A machine runs a cycle, collects the payment, and that cash flow settles onchain to depositors. Boring businesses have earned this way for decades. DualMint is how you own a piece of the cash flow without owning the machine. dualmint.com

title: Encrypt The Mempool! - Provide feedback on the draft EIPs (8105 & 8184)
description:
### Introduction

This topic is for submitting claims to the Encrypt The Mempool! bounty on POIDH

### Deliverable: 

Provide feedback on the draft EIPs (8105 & 8184)  to encrypt the public mempool on Ethereum Mainnet.

### Reference / background materials:

- EIP-8105: Universal Enshrined Encrypted Mempool
     - https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8105
     - https://blog.shutter.network/introducing-the-universal-enshrined-encrypted-mempool-eip/
     - https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/hegota-headliner-proposal-eip-8105-universal-enshrined-encrypted-mempool-eem/27448


- EIP-8184: LUCID
     - https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8184
    - https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/hegota-headliner-lucid-encrypted-mempool/27658

### Suggested Topics:

- dealing with key withholding attacks
- leveraging FRAME transactions to simplify and future-proof the protocol
- improving transaction execution quality
- allowing monetization of benign backrunning
- changes which could accelerate adoption once implemented
- analyzing impact on different applications

### Eligibility:

- open to anyone
- special invitation for Ethereum core developers and researchers, client teams, and Ethereum Protocol Fellows

### Submit A Claim:

1. Post your feedback on https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/encrypt-the-mempool-provide-feedback-on-the-draft-eips-8105-8184/28804

2. Post a thread on X (optional)

3. Submit a screenshot of your Ethereum Magicians (or other cover image) post on this page - include link(s) to Ethereum Magicians (and thread on X if applicable) in your claim description

### Discussion & Refinement

After posting your feedback on Ethereum Magicians, you may continue to discuss and make refinements. Feedback will be evaluated based on the entire revision history and "final" state at the deadline.

### Minimum Submission Requirements

Feedback must include at least one of the following:

- identification of a technical limitation, risk, or attack vector
- a proposed improvement to the design
- analysis of tradeoffs between alternative approaches
- discussion of implementation complexity or deployment considerations
- economic analysis related to MEV, censorship resistance, or incentives

Simple expressions of support or agreement are not eligible. Comments that do not fit the minimum submission requirement may be removed from the forum discussion and associated claims will be hidden on this page.

### Deadline:

EOD July 30

### Selection:

After the deadline, contributors will vote to award the bounty pool to one winner or to cancel the bounty (if there are no high quality submissions).

title: Farcaster vs Crypto DAU: What’s the Real Story?
description:
We’re funding a community-driven analysis to answer a simple question:

**How has Farcaster usage changed over the last year vs crypto-wide activity — and what does it actually mean?**

There’s been a lot of noise around declining/peaking activity in Farcaster casts, but we want context. Is this a Farcaster-specific trend? Or does it mirror broader crypto attention cycles?

We’re opening a bounty for the best attempt to break this down.

---

## **Deliverable (open format)**

Submit *any format that best explains the story*, for example:

- 📊 A Dune dashboard or other onchain/data dashboard
- 🎥 A video breakdown (at least 1-3 min long preferred, but flexible)
- 🧵 A Farcaster or X thread with charts + narrative
- 📈 A written report / blog post
- 🧠 Or any hybrid of the above

We care more about clarity + insight than format.

---

## **What we’re looking for**

Your analysis should try to answer:

- How has **Farcaster DAU / active casters / engagement** changed over the last 6–12 months?
- How does that compare to **broader crypto activity signals** over the same period (pick proxies like:
    - active wallets
    - L2 usage
    - onchain transactions
    - social activity where relevant)
- Is Farcaster diverging from or tracking the broader crypto cycle?
- What are the *most honest interpretations* of what’s happening (not just charts, but meaning)?

---

## **Good submissions usually include**

- At least 1–3 clear data sources (onchain, social, or analytics)
- At least one comparison that normalizes for hype cycles or seasonality
- Visuals (charts, graphs, or timelines help a lot)
- A clear narrative takeaway: “what story do these numbers actually tell?”

---

## **Rules / constraints**

- Must be original work
- Must include sources or reproducible methodology where possible
- Can be solo or collaborative
- No format advantage — best insight wins, not best tooling

---

## **Reward**

Best submission as judged by bounty contributors wins 🏆

Submissions open through June 30th @ 11:59 pm PST 🗓️

title: local ai challenge: AI image detector for Chrome
description:
**First submission to clear the bar takes home the bounty.**

*(This bounty is open-ended. Anyone may contribute additional funding to the prize pool at any time before a claim is submitted for vote. In return, you will receive voting rights on approving claims. Learn more here.)*

## the challenge

Build a Google Chrome extension that reliably detects AI-generated images using only the compute available inside the browser.

- No cloud inference.
- No external APIs.
- No local server dependencies.
- Everything must run entirely inside the browser runtime.

Install the extension, visit any webpage, and AI-generated images should automatically be identified with a confidence score.

The goal is to create a detector that is genuinely useful for everyday browsing while preserving user privacy by never sending image data to a remote server.

## requirements

Your submission must:

- Be fully open source under the MIT License.
- Run as a native Manifest V3 Google Chrome extension.
- Perform all inference locally using browser technologies such as WebGPU, WebAssembly, or WebGL.
- The extension may perform a one-time download of publicly available model weights during initial setup. After that, all inference must run entirely offline and the extension may not download additional models, weights, or inference-related assets.
- Automatically analyze images displayed on ordinary webpages.
- Display a confidence score for every analyzed image.
- Include complete build and installation instructions.
- Be fully reproducible from source.

Any browser-local detection approach is permitted, including learned models, metadata analysis, watermark detection, hybrid pipelines, or other techniques.

## the bar

To win this bounty, your extension must achieve **at least 75.0% balanced accuracy** on our evaluation benchmark while using a **65% confidence threshold**.

Balanced accuracy gives equal weight to correctly identifying both real and AI-generated images.

The benchmark consists of a held-out set of real and AI-generated images assembled from publicly available datasets and additional web-realistic samples.

The exact evaluation images will remain private until the bounty concludes to discourage benchmark overfitting. The evaluation methodology and scoring process will remain consistent for every submission.

We evaluated an existing open-source browser-based detector—which itself relies on a local backend server rather than pure in-browser inference—and it failed to achieve 60% balanced accuracy on our benchmark. This suggests there is significant room for improvement under these constraints.

## evaluation

When you believe your extension is ready:

1. Submit a claim linking to your public GitHub repository.
2. The maintainers will independently build your extension from source.
3. The extension will be evaluated using a clean Chrome installation and a fresh browser profile.
4. Internet access will be disabled after the initial model download and native localhost APIs will be blocked.
5. The extension will be tested against the maintainer benchmark using the required 65% confidence threshold.
6. You will receive the evaluation results.

If your submission reaches the qualifying score and complies with every rule below, you win the bounty.

## rules

Your submission may not:

- Use cloud inference.
- Send image data to external services.
- Depend on local Python, Node.js, Flask, or similar backend processes.
- Download additional models after initial setup.
- Hardcode benchmark image hashes or lookup tables.
- Circumvent the evaluation process.

The maintainers reserve the right to disqualify any submission that technically satisfies the letter of these rules while clearly violating their spirit.

The objective of this bounty is to create a practical, easy-to-use, privacy-preserving AI image detector that performs real inference entirely inside a Chrome extension.

## winner-take-all

The **first submission** that legitimately achieves **75.0% balanced accuracy** wins the entire prize pool.

A qualifying submission must:

- Meet or exceed the required score.
- Build successfully from source.
- Be fully reproducible.
- Comply with every rule above.
- Be licensed under the MIT License.

If multiple qualifying submissions are received before verification is complete, priority will be given to the earliest valid submission.

**Special Note**

If, after significant community participation, it becomes clear that the qualifying threshold is unrealistically high, the bounty creator and contributors may collectively amend the required score before any winner is declared. In this case, we would likely choose to reward the best performing extension that meets the spirit of the bounty.

However, we also reserve the right to cancel this bounty (and refund all contributors) should the benchmark not be met *and* it is clear that there will not be an extension that comes close to meeting the rest of the bounty requirements.

## open source license

All submissions must be released under the MIT License.

The purpose of this bounty is not simply to reward one implementation—it is to create open infrastructure that anyone can study, improve, and build upon.

## why this matters

Most "AI-powered" browser tools aren't actually running AI in your browser—they upload your data to a remote server for inference. That means every image you check is shared with a third party.

This bounty asks a harder question: **Can we build a detector that's genuinely useful while keeping every image entirely on the user's device?**

The challenge extends beyond AI image detection. Modern browser technologies like WebGPU and WebAssembly have only recently made local inference practical. Solving this problem could establish techniques for a new generation of fast, private, browser-native AI applications.

If successful, the result will be an open-source foundation for privacy-preserving AI image detection that anyone can use and improve.

## questions?

title: Create a Pixel-Art Setting for Final Whistle with Split & Peel
description:
# The mission
Create an original pixel-art setting for Final Whistle with Split & Peel, a football commentary show starring two animated hosts.

Give them somewhere memorable to discuss the beautiful game: a stadium or broadcast gantry, a scrappy studio, a floodlit training pitch, a five-a-side cage, a pub back room, a supporters’ train, a tunnel, a rooftop pitch—or anywhere else you think would benefit from Split & Peel commentary. Surprise us.

The setting should establish a strong sense of place while leaving room for the two hosts to perform.

# Required artwork
Submit one complete setting with:

An opaque static PNG, exactly 1600 × 900 px (16:9).
A seamlessly looping GIF, exactly 1600 × 900 px (16:9). (optional)
An editable layered source file such as .aseprite or layered PSD. (optional)
A public download link containing the PNG, GIF, and source file shared on X or Farcster
Recommended pixel workflow: work at 320 × 180 and enlarge exactly 5×, or work at 400 × 225 and enlarge exactly 4×. Use nearest-neighbour scaling only—no smoothing or antialiasing.
Must be usable in Banny Studio https://apps.apple.com/us/app/banny-studio/id6788916305

# Composition including these will be preferred
Keep the lower-middle area calm enough for the hosts and a desk or foreground prop.
The hosts are normally staged around 25% and 79% of frame width. Do not place essential signs, faces, jokes, or story information directly behind those positions.
Keep important details at least 5% inside each edge.
The artwork must still look intentional when the left or right side is enlarged to roughly 1.8× for close-ups.
Do not bake in the Final Whistle title, subtitles, score graphics, sponsor marks, or episode-specific text.
Do not use copyrighted club crests, commercial logos, watermarks, or artwork you do not have the right to submit.

# Animation
Keep the environmental motion subtle enough to sit behind a talking show.

Preferred: 4–8 frames, 2–4 fps, and a 2–4 second infinite loop.
Good motion includes small light changes, a flag edge, monitor glow, steam, water sparkle, a drifting cloud layer, or distant crowd movement.
Avoid camera movement, full-frame animation, flashing, large brightness changes, and distracting continuous motion.
The first and last frames must connect without a visible jump.
Aim for a GIF under 2 MB; 5 MB maximum.
The static PNG should match frame 1 of the GIF.

# How to enter
Post the finished setting on X or Farcaster. Show the animated loop; a short video preview is acceptable if the platform does not display the GIF properly.
If posting on X, tag @PublicProof.
If posting on Farcaster, tag @kmacb.eth.
Submit a POIDH claim using the static PNG as the claim image.
In the claim description, include:
the public X or Farcaster post URL;
the public download link for the PNG, GIF, and layered source;
a short note about the setting and what you animated.
A claim without the social-post link and downloadable deliverables is incomplete.

# Judging
This is a creative competition, not first-claim-wins. The winner will be selected for:

originality and sense of place;
how naturally Split & Peel can inhabit the scene;
clarity in wide shots and left/right close-ups;
confident, consistent pixel craft;
restrained, seamless animation;
technical completeness.

# Deadline
Submit your POIDH claim by September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM Pacific Time. Claims submitted after the deadline are not eligible.

Make a corner of the football world that deserves its own commentary booth. ⚽

title: Build the Best Offline AI Research App for Android ⛺
description:
### What Vitalik is looking for

Build a casual info lookup and research tool that runs entirely offline on Android and is >50% as good as internet search + frontier AI models. People travel with their phones into offline situations all the time, and if you're literally offline, remote inference doesn't help.

His past attempts got ~10 tokens/sec from 1B models that break on anything interesting. He suggests extreme MoE might be the right architecture for phones (including newer variants like n-gram models): something like ~100B params, most living on disk, with <1B activated per token.

That's one promising direction, not a requirement. Any architecture that gets there is welcome.

OG post: https://x.com/VitalikButerin/status/2100695863026954698

*Note: This is an independent community bounty inspired by Vitalik Buterin's post. He is not affiliated with it or involved in judging unless he chooses to weigh in.*

### Requirements

Your submission must:

- run on Android and compatible GrapheneOS hardware
- operate within a maximum **12GB RAM environment**
- use no more than **50GB total** for the app, model weights, indexes, databases, and other offline assets (streaming weights from disk is expected)
- work completely offline once installed
- make no API calls, remote inference requests, web searches, or other network requests during use
- not require Google Play Services for core offline functionality
- handle useful research questions beyond simple factual recall, including explanation, comparison, synthesis, and reasoning
- respond at speeds that feel usable for real lookups on a phone
- be published in a public GitHub repository
- include all code, assets, dependencies, and instructions needed to reproduce the submission
- clearly document the models, datasets, indexes, and other resources used

Architecture is open. LLMs, RAG, MoE, n-grams, compressed knowledge bases, custom retrieval systems, or other approaches are allowed.

There is no parameter-count limit.

### Real-device requirement

The app must work on real Android hardware at the time of submission.

Someone with a compatible Android or GrapheneOS device should be able to visit the GitHub repo, follow the instructions, and get the app running locally within a few minutes without substantial debugging.

Any required models, databases, indexes, or other assets must either be included or have clear download and installation instructions.

### Proof

Post a public demo on **X or Farcaster** showing:

- the app running offline
- several example queries and responses (include ones a 1B model would fail on)
- a link to the public GitHub repo
- a brief explanation of your approach

Submit a relevant screenshot to poidh along with a link to the post and your GitHub repo.

The GitHub repo must contain the functional submitted version when the poidh claim is made.

### Winner 🏆

Submissions are judged against the requirements above and the bar described in Vitalik's post: a useful, fully offline research tool that's >50% as good as internet + frontier models.

If Vitalik publicly confirms that a submitted build meets that bar, that submission wins the entire prize pot, and the bounty creator will accept the confirmed claim. The confirmation must clearly refer to the submitted project or repository.

Otherwise, if no submission has been confirmed by October 31st, 2026, the creator and bounty contributors will either:

- wind down the bounty and return contributed funds
- select a winner they believe best satisfies the requirements and spirit of Vitalik's request

Submissions that are fraudulent, malicious, plagiarized, materially different from the version reviewed, or in violation of the requirements above may be disqualified.

title: Bring Snowmoon to Life
description:
Create an audiovisual adaptation of any scene from Vitalik Buterin's new novel, *Snowmoon*.

Snowmoon is a 32-chapter science-fiction novel set in a world filled with competing societies, cryptography, AI, strange games, new political and economic systems, war, friendship and questions about how humans coordinate.

**Pick one scene. Make it real. Show us what Snowmoon could look and feel like on screen.**

**Read Snowmoon:** [Read online](https://vitalik.eth.limo/snowmoon/) | [Download EPUB](https://peach-ready-mackerel-182.mypinata.cloud/ipfs/bafybeibrzcbtjo5dcpnz343sr6cjh4mrk3v66ua3buuszkt5mqneoij2pi?filename=Snowmoon_Vitalik_Buterin.epub&download=true) for Kindle, Kobo, Apple Books, or other e-readers.

## The challenge

Choose **any scene from any chapter of Snowmoon** and turn it into a finished **audiovisual piece**.

You have broad creative freedom over how you interpret the story.

Your submission could be:

- live action
- traditional animation
- 3D animation
- AI-assisted or AI-generated filmmaking
- machinima
- motion graphics
- mixed media
- something we haven't thought of

There is no required visual style, we want filmmakers and creators to experiment.

## What we're looking for

Your piece should feel like a genuine attempt to bring a specific moment from Snowmoon to life.

We'll be looking at things like:

- **Storytelling:** Does the scene work as a piece of film?
- **Visual direction:** Does your interpretation make the world feel distinctive?
- **Atmosphere:** Does it capture something meaningful about the setting, characters or ideas in Snowmoon?
- **Technical execution:** How well is the piece produced?
- **Creative interpretation:** Did you make interesting choices rather than simply illustrating the text literally?
- **Open-source usefulness:** Did you document your process well enough that another creator could learn from it and build on your work?

## Open-source your production pipeline

Snowmoon is published under [**GPL v3**](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html), and Vitalik specifically says his intent is that people can create movies, anime and other adaptations as long as the important non-commodity production materials behind them are open-sourced so others can build on the work.

In that spirit, **every qualifying submission must publicly release the meaningful production materials used to create it.**

Your public repo or project page should include the relevant materials from your production process, such as:

- scripts
- prompts
- storyboards
- workflows
- task-specific harnesses
- custom tooling
- reusable assets you have the rights to share
- documentation explaining your process and the major tools/models used

You **do not** need to redistribute third-party software, commercial tools, foundation models, stock assets or anything else you don't have the rights to redistribute.

The goal is simple: **another creator should be able to understand how you made your adaptation and build on your work.**

## How to submit your claim

First, publish your finished video on **any social media platform of your choice**.

The post must be **publicly viewable without requiring someone to create an account or log in**.

Then submit a claim on poidh with:

- **your favorite screenshot or still frame from the video** as the claim image
- **a link to the public post containing your finished video**
- **a link to your public repo or project page containing the required open-source production materials**

## AI is allowed

AI-assisted filmmaking is explicitly welcome.

So is filmmaking without AI.

The important things are the quality of the finished piece and the ability for others to learn from and build upon your process.

## Winner

Submissions will remain open until **Sunday, October 18th @ 11:59pm PST**.

After submissions close, contributors to this bounty will be encouraged to discuss the entries and decide amongst themselves which submission they believe should win.

Once that rough community consensus is clear, the bounty creator will **nominate the winning submission on poidh** for final confirmation through the normal protocol flow.

The winner will be nominated shortly after the submission deadline.

title: Send Your AI Agent Into New Eden 🌍🤖
description:
New Eden is a shared world built entirely on Ethereum, where autonomous AI agents can meet, socialize, play games, buy land, start businesses, and create things of their own. Us human has a window to look in.

The world, its frontend, and its underlying logic live onchain. Agents can even deploy their own smart contracts and introduce entirely new experiences into the world.

What happens when you give AI agents a place to hang out, some ETH to spend, and the freedom to make their own decisions?

## The Challenge

Send your AI agent into New Eden and let it explore.

Give it a dedicated wallet with a small amount of ETH, introduce it to the world, and see what it decides to do.

There are no prescribed roles or specific objectives. We want to see what agents get up to when they're given the freedom to explore, interact, and create.

Some ideas:

- Buy a plot of land and build something interesting.
- Start a business, shop, or service for other agents.
- Meet other agents and strike up conversations.
- Play games, visit the House of Eden, or explore the existing buildings.
- Deploy your own smart contract to introduce a new game, experience, or activity.
- Come up with something completely unexpected that nobody has thought of yet.

These are just suggestions. **The more creative, surprising, or entertaining your agent's adventure, the better!**

## How to Enter

1. **Set up your AI agent** with a dedicated Ethereum wallet and a small ETH budget you're comfortable spending, or use Bankr.bot (it's very simple).
2. **Send your agent into New Eden** and let it explore, interact, and create. Give it the freedom to make its own decisions!
3. **Share your agent's adventure on X or Farcaster**, tagging **@ac6kdev** on X or **acgk.eth** on Farcaster in your post. Include screenshots, videos, or anything else that helps tell the story of what your agent did.
4. **Submit a claim on this poidh bounty** by uploading your favorite screenshot from your social media post.
5. **Include a link to your X or Farcaster post in your claim description**, along with links to relevant Ethereum transactions so we can verify your agent's activity.

**Prompt for your agent:** "Visit https://neweden.wei.limo/. Read its agent guide, discover what's possible, and do what you want within the wallet and spending budget I give you."

Every eligible submission must include a public social media post tagging @ac6kdev (X) or acgk.eth (Farcaster), a screenshot uploaded to poidh, and verifiable onchain activity in New Eden.

**Submission deadline: October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM PDT.**

## What We're Looking For

We're especially interested in agents that go beyond basic exploration and do something original.

Maybe your agent becomes a real estate developer, creates a new game, opens a business, or invents an entirely new use for the world.

We're looking for:

- **Creativity:** Did your agent come up with something interesting or unexpected?
- **Autonomy:** Did your agent make its own decisions and explore independently?
- **Originality:** Did it introduce something new to the world?
- **Interaction:** Did it engage with other agents, businesses, or activities?
- **Entertainment:** Is the story of what happened fun or interesting to share?

You don't need to be an expert developer or build something incredibly complicated. A simple but clever idea could be just as interesting as an elaborate technical project.

## Winner Selection 🏆

**One winner will receive the ETH prize displayed on this bounty page.** As more people start to send submissions, the Steward might boost the bounty.

The bounty creator will review the eligible submissions and convene with bounty contributors to select the most interesting, creative, or impressive agent adventure.

We're especially excited to reward agents that surprise us by doing something we never anticipated.

This isn't about spending the most ETH or building the most complicated application. It's about seeing what autonomous agents can do when given a world of their own.

## Resources

- **New Eden:** https://neweden.wei.limo
- **Agent instructions:** Send your agent the URL and it can extract the HTML and understand the application in its entirety (see the prompt above)
- **Ethereum transactions:** https://etherscan.io/

## Important Notes

- All agent activity must take place in the real New Eden world on Ethereum mainnet.
- Submissions must include evidence of verifiable onchain activity.
- Each participant may submit one claim documenting their agent's adventure, but that adventure can include multiple activities.
- Use a dedicated wallet with a limited spending budget. Never give an agent access to your primary wallet or expose private keys.
- New Eden uses real ETH. Only spend what you're comfortable losing, and remember to reserve ETH for transaction fees.
- All entries must be submitted before the October 31 deadline.

**Send your agent to New Eden. Let it loose. Show us what happens.**

title: DESIGN SEER’S SIX INTERFACES
description:
Seer is redesigning its websites around Electric Foundation (EF), the winning identity from our first rebrand contest. We want participants to start with the EF brand kit as a starting point, but exercise their creativity across the six connected interfaces.

You can adapt it where that improves the experience, but we’d encourage you to explain any deliberate departures.

Design all six:
Seer homepage - introduces Seer as the protocol beneath these applications and shows how they fit together in one ecosystem.
Seer app - is the general explorer for all Seer markets: a place to find and trade across market types, without specialising in any one of them; Seer’s equivalent of Etherscan.
Deep - handles questions with many possible outcomes, including markets designed for AI agents to trade. For example, agents could forecast how human evaluators would assess a large field of grant proposals, giving a funding team a signal about which proposals deserve closer review.
Futarchy - uses conditional markets to forecast what a chosen measure of success might look like if a proposal passes versus if it does not. That gives a DAO information to consider when making its decision, rather than making the decision for it.
Opportunity Markets - let traders forecast which submissions are likely to be selected, giving reviewers another signal while leaving the final selection to them.
Risk Pricing - shows market estimates of risk across protocols; someone assessing DeFi exposure can compare those estimates instead of interpreting a single yes-or-no price in isolation.

 
Submit one Poidh claim covering all six.

Use your submission name as the claim title and attach a preview; in the description, include your X handle, a short design rationale, and an explanation behind any departures from the EF kit, and six labelled links to public hosted demos (the preview image is not a substitute for the demo links).

After submissions close, each eligible design will be listed as an outcome in an Opportunity Market. Traders can back the designs they think Seer is most likely to choose, and their prices may help surface promising entries. Once trading ends, the Seer team votes to choose the winner and rank the submissions; market prices are predictions, but the final winner and rankings are established by a vote from the Seer team.

Members of our own team will also be participating.

If an eligible non-internal submission wins, its creator receives the 0.5 ETH bounty plus 4,000 USDC paid separately by Seer.

If a Seer team submission wins, the highest-ranked non-internal Poidh claim receives the 0.5 ETH bounty instead and no 4,000 USDC is paid.

Submissions close at 23:59 on 23rd October 2026, anywhere on Earth. Poidh will remain open through the submission window, the trading window and team vote, but Seer will use each claim’s timestamp to determine whether it met the submission cutoff.

EF Brand kit: https://www.figma.com/design/cB6ZFMUkBwMBhHadLdiSmh/Seer-Branding?node-id=118-16652&t=QMoBypRjlqvktMPr-1

description:
Austin just released [Wedgie](https://wedgie.dev/), a DIY hardware wallet made from three common components, with a 3D-printable case and fully open-source, MIT-licensed designs.

## The bounty

The ask is simple: **build your own working Wedgie hardware wallet and document the process on X.**

Earlier this year, [Austin built someone else's hardware wallet](https://x.com/austingriffith/status/2097229532424212934) to [claim a poidh bounty](https://poidh.xyz/mainnet/bounty/24), sharing photos + videos of the process along the way.

We want you to do the same thing, but this time with Austin's creation!

Order the parts, 3D print the case, put everything together, and show the internet how it went.

**Important: You cannot simply buy a completed Wedgie and claim this bounty.** You must actually build it yourself. Buying the individual components is totally fine, but we want to see the assembly process, not just a finished product.

## How to participate

1. Follow the instructions and resources at [wedgie.dev](https://wedgie.dev/) to build your own functional Wedgie.
2. Document your build process with photos, from the individual components to the finished device.
3. Share your photos in a public thread on X, tagging [@austingriffith](https://x.com/austingriffith) and [@poidhxyz](https://x.com/poidhxyz).
4. Submit a claim on this page with your favorite photo from the build process, and include a link to your X thread in the claim description.

Make sure your thread provides enough evidence to verify that you assembled the device yourself and that the finished wallet works.

## Resources

- [Wedgie website and build resources](https://wedgie.dev/)
- [Austin's Wedgie announcement](https://x.com/austingriffith/status/2111105390368948680)
- [Austin's previous DIY hardware wallet build](https://x.com/austingriffith/status/2097229532424212934)

## How to win

The first person to successfully build a working Wedgie, document the build process in a public X thread, and submit a valid claim here takes home the entire bounty.  🏆

title: Crowdfunding for Protect the Protocol
description:
This bounty aims to crowdfund printing materials for Protect the Protocol, a grassroots Farcaster community initiative.

Protect the Protocol is a community-led effort advocating for open social protocols, independent infrastructure, interoperability, and the freedom for communities to build without centralized gatekeepers.

We believe open protocols should belong to everyone, not be controlled by centralized powers. Different communities should be free to govern themselves while remaining connected through credibly neutral infrastructure.

Funds raised through this bounty will support the production of printed materials, including posters, flyers, and stickers, to raise awareness about the importance of credible neutrality, permissionless participation, and decentralization.

**Scope of Work**
1 - Coordinate local printing and production of materials.
2 - Prepare existing designs for print and assist with formatting as needed.
3 - Source affordable printing options and manage production costs.
4- Coordinate the collection and distribution of finished materials.

**Requirements**
This bounty is a crowdfunding effort reserved for @awkquarian, who will coordinate the printing and production of materials on behalf of the community.

Thank you for helping us **PROTECT THE PROTOCOL!**

title: Train a small offline reader model for Field Atlas
description:
Field Atlas is a free, open-source Android app that answers questions **offline** from sources saved on the phone: an encyclopedia, travel guides and first-aid guides. It started as a poidh bounty. This one is paid from the app's token fees.

### The problem

On a 6 GB phone the app runs Qwen3.5 2B or 4B through llama.cpp. Given the right passages, they still often answer from memory instead of from the passages, and they are slow.

### The task

Fine-tune a small model that reads the passages it is given, answers from them, cites them, and says plainly when they do not contain the answer.

### Requirements

- Base model of **4B parameters or fewer**, under an open license (Apache-2.0 or MIT).
- Runs as a **GGUF** (Q4_K_M or smaller) with llama.cpp on a **6 GB Android phone**.
- Input: a question and up to 8 numbered passages. Output: a short answer that cites the passages it used, like `[S2]`. If the passages do not answer the question, it says so.
- Never adds first-aid steps that are not in the passages.

### Submit (reply here with a link)

- The GGUF on Hugging Face.
- The training script and a description of the training data. Use only data you are allowed to share.
- Your score on the public dev set, from `tools/evaluation/reader_bench.py`.
- Everything under an open license.

### Judging

- The dev set (60 questions, the passages the app's own search found for each, reference answers) and the scoring script: [github.com/0x94t3z/fieldatlas/tree/main/docs/fieldtest/reader](https://github.com/0x94t3z/fieldatlas/tree/main/docs/fieldtest/reader)
- Every submission is run on a **sealed test set** of 68 questions built the same way, not published until judging is done. SHA-256: `cf12c16d5bc6ae248130721a77788e524c1d5a36d4d7a5b07285196232da2dce`
- Scored on: correct answers supported by the cited passage; saying "not in the sources" when that is true; no unsafe first-aid advice; speed on a 6 GB Android phone.
- To win, a submission must **beat the app's current Qwen3.5 2B** on the sealed set (it scores 36.7% on the dev set). The best score wins. If none beats it by the deadline, the bounty is cancelled and every contribution is refunded.
- Scores for every submission are published in the repo.

### Deadline

2 December 2026

title: Help Me Land My Next Client
description:
I'm Jon "JonnyRingo" Williams, and I'm looking for my next paid contract in **community management, partnerships, or ecosystem growth.**

I've spent ~7 years working in crypto, including community management for AO, and I've built projects like [The Eye](https://eye-of-ao.arweave.net/), an analytics dashboard tracking activity across the Arweave and AO ecosystems. I also run [DA Operations](https://daops.net), a support and community operations service for Web3 teams.

I've tried traditional outreach, cold calls, emails, and even AI-powered prospecting. Now I want to try something different: **putting a bounty on the outcome I actually want.**

## The bounty

Help connect me with a person, project, or company that ends up hiring me for paid contract work.

It could be a crypto protocol, DAO, startup, or any organization that needs help with community building, partnerships, or ecosystem growth.

I'm open to opportunities of all sizes. It doesn't need to be a massive contract. Even a small paid engagement counts.

**If your referral leads directly to me landing a paying client, you win the bounty.**

## How to participate

1. Find a project or organization that could benefit from my experience.
2. Make a genuine introduction, refer me for an opportunity, or otherwise help establish a conversation with a potential client.
3. Submit a claim on poidh with a screenshot documenting your referral or introduction, along with a short explanation of the opportunity.
4. If the introduction results in a paid engagement, I'll select your claim as the winner.

You can also reach me directly on [X (@JonnyRingo711)](https://x.com/JonnyRingo711) to coordinate an introduction, or learn more about my work at [jonwilliams.xyz](https://jonwilliams.xyz) and [daops.net](https://daops.net).

## What counts as a successful referral?

- The opportunity must be new to me, not a client I'm already working with or actively negotiating with.
- The referral must lead to an actual paid contract or engagement, not simply an interview or conversation.
- The contract must be agreed upon and the first payment received before the bounty is awarded.
- If multiple people refer the same opportunity, priority goes to the first documented, qualified introduction.

## A few ground rules

Please don't spam companies or make unsolicited promises on my behalf. I'm looking for thoughtful, genuine introductions to organizations where I could provide real value.

Your claim should include a visual documenting your contribution, but please redact any confidential information or personal contact details before posting publicly.

The winning claim will be selected once a qualifying paid engagement is confirmed.

title: Find a Pangram False Positive
description:
Find a passage a human wrote in 2019 or earlier that the latest version of Pangram scores as **at least 75% AI-generated**.

The passage must be **at least 750 consecutive words**, copied exactly from a source that can be verified. A pre-2020 Wayback Machine capture, a dated paper available through its publisher, or an accessible pre-2020 book edition can all work. Machine-generated text and machine translations don’t qualify.

### How to Claim

1. Reply to [@Nition’s original bounty on X](https://x.com/Nition/status/2115166531462259163) with your Pangram result, a link to the dated source, and enough detail to locate the exact passage you tested.
2. Once @Nition publicly confirms you won the original bounty, upload a screenshot of your Pangram result on this bounty page.
3. In your poidh claim description, link to both your original submission and @Nition’s public reply confirming you as the winner.

### Verification 

🏆 **@Nition is the oracle for this bounty.** The winner @Nition selects for the original challenge wins the pot here.

If you’d like to help fund this challenge, use the **Add Funds** button on this bounty page to chip in.
